t: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query — Editorial
o: Each query asks: among all intervals containing the point (endpoints inclusive), how small is the shortest one — or -1 if nothing covers it. In example 1, point 4 lies inside [1,4], [2,4], [3,6] and [4,4]; the winner is [4,4] with size 1. Point 5 is covered only by [3,6], giving 6 - 3 + 1 = 4. Testing every interval for every point is O(n*q) — around 10^10 operations at the stated limits of 10^5 intervals and queries — so we process offline instead: sort the queries ascending, sweep a pointer over interval left endpoints, and keep currently active intervals in a min-heap ordered by size. Intervals whose right end has fallen behind the current query are lazily popped, so the heap top is always the smallest live interval; the sweep emits 3, 3, 1, 4 for example 1.
k: Sorting queries turns independent searches into one sweep: each interval is inserted exactly once, when the sweep passes its left endpoint.
A min-heap keyed by (size, right) with lazy eviction of expired right ends answers "smallest active interval" in amortized O(log n).
Sort queries WITH their original indices — answers must be written back in input order.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute Force Scan per Query
a.i: For each query, linearly test every interval for containment and keep the minimum size. This is a direct translation of the statement and is only viable for tiny inputs.
s: For each query q, iterate over all intervals [l, r].
If l <= q <= r, consider r - l + 1 as a candidate answer.
Output the minimum candidate, or -1 when no interval contained q.
a.t: O(n*q) — every interval is checked against every query

a.n: Approach 2: Offline Sweep with a Size-Ordered Min-Heap
a.i: Sort intervals by left end and sort queries ascending while remembering each index. Sweep the sorted queries; before answering one, push every interval whose left end has been passed as a (size, right) pair, then pop pairs whose right end is below the current query — they can never cover this or any later point. The heap top then holds the smallest live interval covering the query.
s: Sort intervals by left endpoint; sort (query, index) pairs by query value.
For each query q in order, push all intervals with left <= q as (r - l + 1, r).
Pop heap entries with right < q (stale intervals).
The remaining top gives the answer for that query index, or -1 if the heap is empty.
Restore answers to their original positions.
a.t: O((n + q) log(n + q)) — two sorts plus amortized heap work; each interval is pushed once and popped at most once
a.sp: O(n + q) — heap contents and the indexed query order

w: Use the offline sweep — it is the intended solution, and its sort-events-plus-heap skeleton recurs in problems like meeting rooms II and closest room. Pitfalls: intervals are INCLUSIVE on both ends, so evict while right < q (not <=); remember to carry original query indices through the sort; store (size, right) tuples so equal sizes compare deterministically. Follow-ups: answer queries online (a segment tree over coordinate-compressed points storing minimum size), or support interval insertion/deletion between queries.
